session.question: How is the SDG Index used to measur progres toward the SDGs at local and regional level in Romania, and what did the results show?
session.answer:
The SDG Index in Romania serves as a quantitative measure for assessing progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at local and regional levels through an integrated approach utilizing 90 indicators stored in a PostgreSQL database. The findings indicate a significant interest among regions in implementing the SDGs; however, many lack defined subnational indicators necessary for comprehensive assessment (unknownauthorsUnknownyearindicator‐basedassessmentof chunk 1). The results of the SDG Index reveal a concentration of sustainable development performance in select geographic areas, with rural and peripheral regions in the eastern and southern regions of Romania identified as the least effective in achieving the SDGs (unknownauthorsUnknownyearindicator‐basedassessmentof chunk 1).

The broader application of the SDG framework for environmental monitoring among European regions, as discussed in the second source, underlines the necessity of local and regional actions, emphasizing the development of diverse indicators beyond mere carbon metrics to include biodiversity and pollution (unknownauthorsUnknownyearenvironmentalmonitoringin chunk 1). While the third source focuses on economic prosperity and sustainability, it reiterates the role of transparency in public policy for effective regional development, although it does not specifically address the use of the SDG Index (unknownauthorsUnknownyearregionaldevelopmentin chunk 1). Thus, while the SDG Index is a vital tool for monitoring progress, its implementation at the regional level remains inconsistent and varies significantly across geographic areas (unknownauthorsUnknownyearindicator‐basedassessmentof chunk 1).
